possible_indirect.limits: Paths are static possibilities. At most 12 shortest path examples are shown; complete indirect module IDs and counts are retained. Trigger activation requires matching events and runtime execution.

contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Compute a selected dashboard count, stored-data formula, fixed baseline or timestamp interval.
inputs_defaults: kpiType nvarchar(50), identifier numeric(9), warehouse nvarchar(25), todaysDateWithWarehouseOffset DATE, todaysDate DATETIME; required, no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: NULL/unknown type or identifier retains0. Missing dates/warehouse can produce zero counts, NULL expressions or timezone errors depending on branch; there is no universal missing-input contract.
Appointment joins can multiply receipt rows; counts are not DISTINCT receipt IDs. The container-rate join can multiply containers across multiple appointments.

Scalar DASHBOARD_DATA lookup can returnNULL, fail on duplicate rows or fail numeric conversion. Residual CASE only clamps negative, so NULL residual remainsNULL; percentage totalNULL takes ELSE0 and can mask missing data.
Week filters use CAST date BETWEEN start and end+1 inclusively, including that additional calendar boundary. DATEFIRST affects called week helpers.

Shortest dock interval returns0 for a single interval and also resets to0 when equal to stored longest; longest no-row default1, average no-row default0. These different fallbacks are not observed measurements.

Work upper bound is UTC start+24h, not separately converted next local midnight; it can differ from a local calendar day at DST transitions. Remaining age<=24 has no lower bound and permits negative elapsed values. NULL condition does not satisfy <>Closed.
output_shape: nvarchar(50); numeric results converted to text. Initialized0 is retained for unmatched type/identifier; selected branches can assignNULL.

ordered_branches.explanation: Initialize output0; select one case-sensitive/collation-dependent type branch Shipping, Receiving, Labor or Work and then one identifier branch. Unknown identifiers leave0.
Shipping branch counts scheduled/due/late/status-range shipment rows, calculates stored dashboard residual, or count per elapsed local-day hours. IDs310 and330 return fixed150 and970.

Receiving branch uses appointment-date fallback to scheduled receipt date for several counts, stored dashboard residual, closed-receipt unitize-to-close intervals and container-count/hour metric. IDs50,70,710 return fixed102,1475,0.5.
Labor identifier660 counts distinct currently non-logged-off user names through USER_PROFILE.DEFAULT_WHS and logon calendar-date predicate.

Work branch resolves warehouse timezone, converts supplied local date midnight to UTC and adds exactly one day for upper bound. It counts Header instructions by typed Receipt/Cycle Count/Replenishment/picking categories, Closed condition and end interval, or nonclosed aging<=24/>24 conditions.

Work total/percentage identifiers read previously stored DASHBOARD_DATA values with independent scalar subqueries. Percentage returns numerator*100/total only if total>0, else0. Return selected text value without persistent mutation.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: No persistent status, inventory quantity or permissions mutation; output is the stated scalar or returned table.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: Hard-coded type/identifier/status formulas, warehouse timezone and existing DASHBOARD_DATA values. Caller supplies both date representations; no clock consistency check.
Staff default warehouse is a profile setting, not current operating warehouse or authorization. Picking includes Shipment and a second coded category whose exact literal remains withheld.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH or validation result. Invalid timezone, duplicate scalar dashboard rows, nonnumeric stored VALUE, numeric/datetime overflow and called-function failures propagate. Multiple reads have no body-owned snapshot.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: No persistent mutation or lock protocol; reads, if any, follow caller/session isolation. Function result is not evidence of caller authorization or process execution.
contract.trigger_behavior: No persistent DML or DML trigger activation in this body.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: This computes snapshot/helper formulas; it does not execute work, measure complete functional flow duration or prove current metrics. No KPI was operationally executed. Root independently read the same553-line body and supplied corroborating branch observations; author also read it fully.

evidence.description: Complete module body reviewed with original-definition fingerprint.
Shipping identifier formulas and fixed baselines.
Receiving joins, intervals, residuals and baseline constants.

Shipping.formula: Count scheduled today OR scheduled<=today with creation age>24h and trailing<600; warehouse filter applies to either.
Fixed150 and970 respectively; not measured baseline.
Count scheduled DATE in inclusive week-start through week-end+1.
Scheduled-today trailing>=600 count divided by local elapsed day hours when hours>0, else0.

Receiving.formula: Appointment/scheduled date today OR <=today with creation age>24h; CLOSE_DATE NULL.
Appointment/scheduled date today and close calendar date today.
Appointment/scheduled date inclusive week-start through end+1.
Shortest unitize-to-close hours for closed today, but single interval or equality with stored90 returns0; no data0.
Maximum unitize-to-close hours for closed today; no data1.
Average unitize-to-close hours for closed today; no data0.
Joined status900 receipt-container/appointment rows dated today divided by positive local elapsed day hours; otherwise0.

Labor.formula: Distinct USER_ACTIVITY usernames with logon date<=supplied now date, logoffNULL and profile default warehouse.

Work.formula: Closed Header work from WORK_INSTRUCTION_VIEW ending in [converted UTC midnight,start+24h); typed receipt,count,replenishment,picking respectively.
Nonclosed Header work from live table; aging<end and elapsed age<=24h; no lower bound.
Nonclosed Header work elapsed age>24h; no day-end bound.
Stored processed+remaining+at-risk triples for receipt,count,replenishment,picking respectively.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
